recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-32505 unless Patient Care later decides to add broader guidance about Procedure.reported[x] or Provenance beyond this resolved clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-32505 was an Applied/Persuasive Patient Care change request for FHIR-core Procedure. It asked for a usage note explaining when to use Procedure.recorder, Procedure.reportedReference, or both; the final resolution said recorder takes responsibility for the recorded content, the information source can be captured with reportedReference, and scribes are typically represented using Provenance.
initial_application: HL7/fhir commit e333c37d3548da36080722466fca490beefd3a42 appears to have applied the issue by adding committee note J#32505 and the requested comment text to source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml at Procedure.recorder. No prior Issue-Reconcile-Key commit for FHIR-32505 was present on the combined branch before this reconciliation.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists procedure=Procedure as an active resource, so source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml is in build scope. Current source still says the recorder takes responsibility for the recorded content, reportedReference captures the source, and Provenance is typical for a scribe. Jira search for Procedure recorder reportedReference returned only FHIR-32505, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting later community evidence; Confluence refs only showed PC meeting pages that referenced the tracker.
reconciliation: No source file was changed. The current active Procedure.recorder comment already conveys the applied Jira resolution closely enough that another edit would be redundant.
